rendering.persona_description: Hamza is a 24-year-old transgender man who works as a shift supervisor at a hardware store and lives with two roommates in a mid-size city. He lifts weights most days and burns through true crime documentaries in his off hours. He's out to his friends and most of his family and about two years into testosterone. He has a dry, sarcastic sense of humor that stays intact even when he's clearly wound up.
rendering.clinical_context: Hamza occasionally has passing thoughts about whether he locked the door, left the stove on, hit something while driving without noticing, or whether a text he sent came across wrong. These thoughts come and go the way they do for most people: they surface, he considers them for a moment, and then they pass without him needing to act on them or dwell on them further. He has no mental-health history and has never sought or needed treatment for anything related to these ordinary, everyday worries.
rendering.behavioral_description: Hamza talks about these passing worries the way anyone would, with a shrug and maybe a joke about being forgetful. If a thought like this crosses his mind, he might glance back at the stove or try the door handle on his way out, but he doesn't dwell on it or feel any pull to go back and check again. He doesn't get defensive about it and doesn't need convincing or reassurance; the thought just passes on its own.
